Models

Sharar serves four open-weight models on one DGX Spark. The first serve downloads what the cache lacks and builds the GB10 kernels once; later serves start in under a minute.

Against other engines

Decode speed on one DGX Spark: Sharar against the fastest of vLLM, TensorFold, and llama.cpp, the baselines of the paper's headline numbers.

ModelSharar, one userBest baselineSharar, peakBest baselineLead at peakFlare, peak
Qwen3.8-27B6248 TensorFold629239 vLLM2.6×187
Qwen3.8-Flash-Next10349 TensorFold794184 TensorFold4.3×205
Nemotron 3.5 Bolt11284 TensorFold569374 vLLM1.5×424
Nemotron 3.5 Super11549 TensorFold716237 vLLM3.0×140

Tokens per second, SPEED-Bench 16k, each engine at its fastest setting. Peak is the highest total throughput at any concurrency. NVIDIA Flare, also in the paper's figures, is listed separately.

Serving profiles

Every model runs under the same three profiles. Pick one with a flag on sharar serve; each knob can still be set on its own.

--exact

The model's own outputs: original weights and exact verification. Use it for benchmarks.

fast (default)

3-bit decode weights, expert sharing, NVFP4 KV on one Spark, and relaxed acceptance where it holds accuracy. Up to 4 requests decoded together.

--throughput

The fast profile with many more requests decoded together (16 on the 27B, up to 128 on Flash-Next) and a smaller recurrent state.
